# Vamp — chord progression sketchpad

> Vamp is a free, local-first web app for sketching chord progressions and looping a
> backing track (sampled chords, bass and drums) to improvise over. It runs at
> https://rickgroot.github.io/vamp/ with no account, no server and no upload: songs live
> in the browser. This file is written for AI assistants. It explains the JSON a user can
> paste into Vamp, so that when someone asks you for a progression "for Vamp" you can
> answer with exactly that JSON.

## If a user asks you for a Vamp song

Follow these rules; they are what makes the result paste cleanly.

1. **Reply with the JSON and nothing else.** No introduction, no explanation, no comments
   inside the JSON. Wrapping it in a single markdown code fence is fine (Vamp strips it).
2. **One song = one JSON object** in the shape below. Several songs = a backup envelope:
   `{ "app": "vamp", "progressions": [ ...songs ] }`. Vamp opens the first song and saves
   all of them to its library. (A backup exported from Vamp may also carry a `drills` array
   — the user's own practice patterns. Leave it out when you write one; if you are editing a
   backup a user gave you, pass it through untouched.)
3. **Do not include `id`, `createdAt` or `updatedAt`.** Vamp generates them. A copied `id`
   that matches a song the user already saved would overwrite that song.
4. **The beats in a bar add up to `timeSignature.numerator`.** A whole bar in 4/4 is
   `"beats": 4`; two chords in that bar are `2` + `2`; a whole bar in 3/4 is `3`; in 6/8 it
   is `6` (six eighth-note beats).
5. **1 to 4 chords per bar.** Need more changes? Use more bars.
6. **Chord symbols are plain ASCII**: `Bb`, `F#`, `Ebmaj7`, never `♭` or `♯`. No spaces, no
   parentheses, one chord per slot. A rest is the empty string `""`.
7. **Write the song in the key the user asked for.** There is no key field; Vamp infers the
   key from the chords. Users can transpose inside the app.
8. Unless asked otherwise, choose a `tempo`, `instrument` and `groove` that fit the style
   (see "Style suggestions" below).
9. **Before you answer, check your work**: valid JSON, every bar adds up, every symbol is in
   the list below or built from it.

If the user does not know how to load it, tell them separately from the JSON: in Vamp open
**File → Paste JSON…**, paste, press **Import**. The song appears on the canvas and is saved
to the library; **Space** plays it. A saved `.json` file also works via **File → Import file…**.

## The song JSON

The complete shape, with every field. Only `bars` is strictly required (everything else has a
default), but a good answer always fills in `name`, `tempo`, `timeSignature`, `instrument`
and `groove`.

```json
{
  "name": "Four-chord loop",
  "tempo": 96,
  "timeSignature": { "numerator": 4, "denominator": 4 },
  "instrument": "piano",
  "groove": {
    "pattern": "block",
    "bass": "root",
    "bassInstrument": "electric",
    "metronome": false,
    "drums": "pop"
  },
  "loopRange": null,
  "bars": [
    { "slots": [{ "chord": "C", "beats": 4 }] },
    { "slots": [{ "chord": "G", "beats": 4 }] },
    { "slots": [{ "chord": "Am", "beats": 4 }] },
    { "slots": [{ "chord": "F", "beats": 4 }] }
  ]
}
```

### Field reference

| Field | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | `"Untitled progression"` | Song title; also used for export file names. |
| `tempo` | integer 20–300 | `100` | Beats per minute, counted in **quarter notes** whatever the time signature (in 6/8 the eighth-note pulse therefore runs at twice the tempo). |
| `timeSignature.numerator` | integer 1–16 | `4` | Beats per bar. |
| `timeSignature.denominator` | `2`, `4`, `8` or `16` | `4` | The beat unit (4 = quarter note, 8 = eighth note). |
| `instrument` | `"piano"` `"guitar"` `"rhodes"` `"pad"` | `"piano"` | Chord sound: grand piano, nylon acoustic guitar, electric piano, warm pad. |
| `groove.pattern` | `"block"` `"strum"` `"arpeggio"` | `"block"` | How each chord is played: sustained block chord, strummed, or arpeggiated. |
| `groove.bass` | `"none"` `"root"` `"alt"` `"walking"` `"octaves"` | `"none"` | Bass line: none · root on strong beats · alternating root/fifth (boom-chuck) · walking quarter notes · root jumping octaves. |
| `groove.bassInstrument` | `"upright"` `"electric"` `"synth"` `"keys"` | `"upright"` | Bass sound; `"keys"` plays the bass on the chord instrument. |
| `groove.drums` | `"none"` `"rock"` `"pop"` `"swing"` `"bossa"` | `"none"` | Drum-kit pattern (TR-808 samples). |
| `groove.metronome` | boolean | `false` | Click on every beat. |
| `bars` | array of bars | one empty bar | The progression, left to right. **Required.** |
| `bars[].slots` | array of 1–4 slots | one rest slot | The chords in that bar, left to right. |
| `bars[].slots[].chord` | string | `""` | A chord symbol as a musician would write it (see below), or `""` for a rest. |
| `bars[].slots[].beats` | number > 0 and ≤ 64 | `4` | Duration in beats of the time signature's beat unit. Fractions such as `1.5` are allowed. The slots of one bar should add up to the numerator. |
| `loopRange` | `{ "startBar": n, "endBar": n }` or `null` | `null` | Zero-based, inclusive bar indices to loop. `null` loops the whole song. |
| `schemaVersion` | `1` | `1` | Optional. The current format version. |

Unknown fields are ignored. Vamp never rejects a song because of a wrong value: an
out-of-range tempo is clamped, an unknown instrument, pattern, bass or drum value falls back
to its default, invalid beats become `4`, and an impossible time signature becomes 4/4. A
sloppy file therefore imports without an error but sounds different from what you intended,
so stick to the values listed above.

### Style suggestions

Pick values that fit the request; the user can change them afterwards.

| Style | instrument | pattern | bass | bassInstrument | drums | tempo |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Jazz standard / bebop | `rhodes` or `piano` | `block` | `walking` | `upright` | `swing` | 120–220 |
| Ballad | `piano` or `pad` | `block` or `arpeggio` | `root` | `upright` | `none` | 60–80 |
| Pop / rock | `piano` or `guitar` | `block` or `strum` | `root` or `alt` | `electric` | `pop` or `rock` | 90–130 |
| Bossa nova / latin | `guitar` | `strum` or `block` | `alt` | `upright` | `bossa` | 120–150 |
| Folk / country | `guitar` | `strum` | `alt` | `upright` | `none` or `pop` | 90–120 |
| Blues | `piano` or `guitar` | `block` | `alt` or `walking` | `electric` | `rock` or `swing` | 90–120 |
| Ambient / scale practice | `pad` | `block` | `root` or `none` | `synth` | `none` | 60–90 |

## Chord symbols

Vamp stores each symbol exactly as written and parses it with the *tonal* music-theory
library when it plays or draws the chord.

- **Roots**: `A` to `G`, with `#` or `b`: `C`, `Db`, `F#`, `Bb`, `Eb`, `Ab`, `C#`, `G#`.
- **Known-good qualities** (shown on C): `C`, `Cm`, `C7`, `Cmaj7`, `Cm7`, `Cm7b5`, `Cdim`, `Cdim7`, `Caug`, `C+`, `Csus2`, `Csus4`, `C7sus4`, `C6`, `Cm6`, `C69`, `Cadd9`, `Cmaj9`, `Cm9`, `C9`, `C11`, `C13`, `Cmaj13`, `Cm11`, `C7b5`, `C7#5`, `C7b9`, `C7#9`, `C7#11`, `C7b13`, `C7alt`, `CmMaj7`, `Cmaj7#11`, `C5`.
- **Slash chords** put the bass note after `/`: `C/E`, `G7/B`, `Dm7/G`, `Am/G`.
- **Rest**: `""` (the empty string) means silence for that slot.
- **Avoid** these. An unrecognised symbol still imports, but it plays as silence and shows
  as invalid in the editor:
  - Unicode accidentals `B♭`, `F♯`: write `Bb`, `F#`.
  - Parentheses `C7(b9)`, `Cm7(b5)`: write `C7b9`, `Cm7b5`.
  - Jazz shorthand `CΔ7`, `Cø7`, `Cm(maj7)`, `Calt`: write `Cmaj7`, `Cm7b5`, `CmMaj7`, `C7alt`.
  - All caps `CMAJ7`: write `Cmaj7`. Never put spaces inside a symbol.
  - No-chord marks `N.C.`: write `""`.
  - Two chords in one slot such as `"Dm7 G7"`: use two slots.

## More examples

A jazz tune with split bars, a four-chord turnaround bar, a slash chord, a rest, and a loop
over the first four bars only:

```json
{
  "name": "ii-V-I workout",
  "tempo": 160,
  "timeSignature": { "numerator": 4, "denominator": 4 },
  "instrument": "rhodes",
  "groove": {
    "pattern": "block",
    "bass": "walking",
    "bassInstrument": "upright",
    "metronome": false,
    "drums": "swing"
  },
  "loopRange": { "startBar": 0, "endBar": 3 },
  "bars": [
    { "slots": [{ "chord": "Dm7", "beats": 4 }] },
    { "slots": [{ "chord": "G7", "beats": 4 }] },
    { "slots": [{ "chord": "Cmaj7", "beats": 2 }, { "chord": "C6", "beats": 2 }] },
    {
      "slots": [
        { "chord": "Em7", "beats": 1 },
        { "chord": "A7", "beats": 1 },
        { "chord": "Dm7", "beats": 1 },
        { "chord": "G7", "beats": 1 }
      ]
    },
    { "slots": [{ "chord": "Dm7", "beats": 4 }] },
    { "slots": [{ "chord": "G7b9", "beats": 4 }] },
    { "slots": [{ "chord": "Cmaj7/E", "beats": 4 }] },
    { "slots": [{ "chord": "Cmaj7", "beats": 2 }, { "chord": "", "beats": 2 }] }
  ]
}
```

A compound meter. 6/8 has six eighth-note beats per bar, so a whole bar is `"beats": 6` and
a half bar is `3`:

```json
{
  "name": "Slow 6/8 ballad",
  "tempo": 72,
  "timeSignature": { "numerator": 6, "denominator": 8 },
  "instrument": "guitar",
  "groove": {
    "pattern": "strum",
    "bass": "alt",
    "bassInstrument": "upright",
    "metronome": false,
    "drums": "none"
  },
  "loopRange": null,
  "bars": [
    { "slots": [{ "chord": "Am", "beats": 6 }] },
    { "slots": [{ "chord": "F", "beats": 6 }] },
    { "slots": [{ "chord": "C", "beats": 6 }] },
    { "slots": [{ "chord": "G", "beats": 3 }, { "chord": "E7", "beats": 3 }] }
  ]
}
```

Several songs at once, in the same envelope Vamp writes when a user exports a backup (the
`"app"` and `"schemaVersion"` keys are optional on import):

```json
{
  "app": "vamp",
  "schemaVersion": 1,
  "progressions": [
    {
      "name": "12-bar blues in A",
      "tempo": 110,
      "timeSignature": { "numerator": 4, "denominator": 4 },
      "instrument": "guitar",
      "groove": {
        "pattern": "block",
        "bass": "alt",
        "bassInstrument": "electric",
        "metronome": false,
        "drums": "rock"
      },
      "loopRange": null,
      "bars": [
        { "slots": [{ "chord": "A7", "beats": 4 }] },
        { "slots": [{ "chord": "A7", "beats": 4 }] },
        { "slots": [{ "chord": "A7", "beats": 4 }] },
        { "slots": [{ "chord": "A7", "beats": 4 }] },
        { "slots": [{ "chord": "D7", "beats": 4 }] },
        { "slots": [{ "chord": "D7", "beats": 4 }] },
        { "slots": [{ "chord": "A7", "beats": 4 }] },
        { "slots": [{ "chord": "A7", "beats": 4 }] },
        { "slots": [{ "chord": "E7", "beats": 4 }] },
        { "slots": [{ "chord": "D7", "beats": 4 }] },
        { "slots": [{ "chord": "A7", "beats": 4 }] },
        { "slots": [{ "chord": "E7", "beats": 4 }] }
      ]
    },
    {
      "name": "Andalusian cadence",
      "tempo": 84,
      "timeSignature": { "numerator": 4, "denominator": 4 },
      "instrument": "pad",
      "groove": {
        "pattern": "block",
        "bass": "root",
        "bassInstrument": "synth",
        "metronome": false,
        "drums": "none"
      },
      "loopRange": null,
      "bars": [
        { "slots": [{ "chord": "Am", "beats": 4 }] },
        { "slots": [{ "chord": "G", "beats": 4 }] },
        { "slots": [{ "chord": "F", "beats": 4 }] },
        { "slots": [{ "chord": "E", "beats": 4 }] }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

## What the format cannot express

- Melody, lyrics or individual notes. Vamp is a chord sketchpad; chords are voiced
  automatically.
- Inversions or specific voicings, beyond a slash bass note.
- Sections, repeats or a form such as AABA. Write the bars out in order.
- Dynamics, tempo changes, or a swing feel beyond `"drums": "swing"`.
- A key signature. It is inferred from the chords.

## About Vamp

Vamp (https://rickgroot.github.io/vamp/) is a free, installable web app (PWA) that works
offline once loaded. Chords are typed into bars with live validation and colour-coding by
quality; the loop plays with a sampled instrument, an optional bass line, drums and a
metronome. Practice tools include a rhythm-section mixer, a trade-solos mode, a drone /
pedal tone, a transposing-instrument view (Bb, Eb, F), scale suggestions per chord,
notation and chord-chart export (PNG, PDF), MIDI and WAV export, and mic recording of your
solo. All data stays in the browser (IndexedDB and localStorage). Share links encode the
same song JSON in the URL hash, but for assistants the JSON above is the reliable way to
hand over a song.

A second workspace at /vamp/practice generates drills to play on your own instrument —
scale patterns, chord-tone arpeggios and guide-tone lines over the changes of the song you
are writing — through every key, fitted to your instrument's range and shown in written
pitch. That workspace has its own format for a *drill*, which this file does not describe:
it is not something an assistant is asked to write, and the song JSON above is unaffected
by it.
